title: A write through a wider shape view stores an object of the wrong class in an anonymous object, and a narrower view's typed read reads the wrong object's memory.
text: `rule:types/shape-type` compares a shape's field types by ordinary assignability, and a shape value is aliased rather than copied. So with `type Narrow = {pet: Dog}; type Wide = {pet: Animal};`, the program `Narrow $n = {pet: new Dog()}; Wide $w = $n; $w->pet = new Animal(); echo $n->pet->legs;` prints a garbage integer. An anonymous object's class is named for its field names alone (`nvs_ir::lower::shape_class_label`), so its slot carries a tag and nothing else, and `Tag::Object` answers for every class. The same holds for an array's elements and a union's arms in such a slot, and for an erased write into one. A declared class's slot is checked in full (`ClassDesc::field_checks`). The user decided the fix: a shape's field types are invariant in the checker, as `array<T>` already is, so `{pet: Dog}` is not assignable to `{pet: Animal}` and the program above does not compile (`nvs_types::expr::assign`'s shape comparison, `crates/nvs-types/src/expr/assign.rs:474`). Nothing changes at run time, and `rule:types/shape-type` says it. Carrying a declared type per anonymous object, and refusing a write through a wider view at run time, were declined: each costs memory per object and a check per write on the request path.
